summary.headline: IOL Chemicals Q2 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to INR795 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4%, with PAT of INR65 crore (up ~117%).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR795 crore, up about 40% YoY, with H1 revenue of INR1,551 crore (up about 39%). EBITDA rose about 80% YoY to INR115 crore, a 14.4% margin (up 321 bps), and PAT more than doubled in H1 to about INR130 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to 25%+ (revised up from 15-20%) and EBITDA margin of 14-15%, and said prices of key products have been stable for 2-3 quarters. Three projects worth about INR500 crore were announced, to be funded from internal accruals.

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen API portfolio grew ~70% YoY in Q2 and reached 45% of pharma revenue (38% a year ago). Ibuprofen remains an important line, with capacity expansion from 12,000 to 18,000 MTPA planned.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Chemicals EBIT contribution rose to ~7% in Q2 from ~1% a year ago, on better realisations, operating efficiencies and procurement. Ethyl Acetate capacity was raised from 1 lakh to 1.2 lakh tonnes; Acetic Anhydride and Ethyl Acetate ran at full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25%+ YoY, revised up from earlier 15-20%; management expects H2 performance similar to H1.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%; long-term sustainable company-wide EBITDA margin of 15-17% cited for FY29 targeting.
Ibuprofen expansion (12,000 to 18,000 MTPA) targeted for commissioning in FY28, with meaningful benefit expected only in FY28-29.
CDMO formulation and specialty chemicals projects expected to commence commercial operations in FY27 per the opening remarks; later clarified as commercialisation in FY28 for CDMO.
Capex planned at INR250 crore for FY27, about half spent in H1. Management said no further borrowing is planned, with the INR200 crore working capital line as the peak requirement.
Management expects other expenses (power, fuel, freight) to ease in Q3 and Q4, with freight cost to be passed on to customers.
capex_capacity: Three projects announced in Q2 totalling about INR500 crore, funded from internal accruals: ibuprofen expansion (12,000 to 18,000 MTPA, backward integrated, FY28), formulation CDMO (1,500 million tablets per year, Europe-focused, FY28 commercialisation), and a dedicated specialty chemicals toll-manufacturing plant (plant nearly commissioned, first batches expected in November 2026).
FY27 capex planned at INR250 crore, with roughly half spent in H1 FY27.

Ibuprofen and major products run at 90-100% capacity utilisation over the last 3-4 quarters. Paracetamol capacity is about 10,800 MT, with a plan to optimise to 100% first. A paracetamol facility of 18,000 MT was mentioned in a question.
Ethyl Acetate capacity raised from 1 lakh to 1.2 lakh tonnes through debottlenecking, not a new plant.
demand_pricing: Ibuprofen prices have been stable for the last 2-3 quarters. Management expects them to hold at similar levels for the next 1-2 quarters and declined to forecast 2-3 year prices.

Order book: big customers typically 4-6 months, average order book 4-6 quarters; cost pass-through clauses are included given volatile raw material prices. Products covered are mainly ibuprofen, paracetamol and metformin.
API customer onboarding takes about 6-8 months to start commercial orders.
CDMO: development is under way with 2-3 customers, mainly European, with existing customers; validation takes about a year including customer approval.
Management could not give a volume/price split of growth, saying the increase reflects price, better utilisation and procurement.
Paracetamol prices were broadly flat QoQ despite higher acetic acid prices (management said acetic acid is not used directly for paracetamol).
Imported raw materials are about 62-63% of total raw material consumption; 60-70% in chemicals (e.g., acetic acid) and 20-22% in API.

qa_highlights.question: Ibuprofen realisation trends and whether the company will benefit in Q3/Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices have been stable for several quarters and are expected to stay flat for 1-2 quarters; the price benefit is already in the P&L, and the new capacity is a strategic move rather than a response to current pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will incremental ibuprofen capacity go to merchant or formulation customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is roughly 50:50 between new customers and internal CDMO consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and borrowing needs for the rest of FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR200 crore working capital line as of 30 September 2026 is the peak requirement, that no further borrowing is planned, and that cash flow and cash on hand are sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 25% growth imply lower H2 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said 25%+ is for the full year on value basis, with H2 expected to perform at a similar level to H1.

qa_highlights.question: What asset turn and margins are expected in CDMO and the overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turn is about 1:3 for chemicals, 1:1 for API and 1:1 to 1:1.25 for CDMO, around 1:1.75 blended. CDMO margins are expected to exceed API margins, but management said it was too early to quantify them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the specialty chemicals toll-manufacturing arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: A renowned global chemical company customer under a cost-plus, long-term tolling arrangement with a dedicated plant; the product is confidential and is not sold in the open market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to about 14.5% of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to higher power and fuel costs in the summer quarter and higher freight cost, and expects these to decline in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Ibuprofen supply additions from peers and China could weigh on realisations once the 18,000 MTPA expansion is commissioned in FY28.
CDMO and specialty chemical ramp-ups depend on customer validation and approvals (about one year for European approval); commercialisation timing has shifted from Q3 FY27 to FY28.
Raw material price volatility and acetic acid spikes; pass-through clauses in contracts are not fully in place. Management could not quantify the ibuprofen price trend beyond 1-2 quarters.
Other expenses rose to about 14.5% of sales (vs 13.7-14% historically); watch whether freight and power costs ease in Q3 and Q4.
Management declined to disclose product-level profitability, volume/price split and API per-kg price changes, which limits analysis.
Triacetin export commercial orders have not yet started despite REACH registration.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H1 performance and FY27 guidance, which was revised up. Cautious and evasive on ibuprofen pricing beyond 1-2 quarters, product-level margins, volume/price split and CDMO margins, citing confidentiality or market dynamism.
key_quotes: We have maintained the positive momentum during the second quarter of FY27, delivering healthy growth across our businesses, accompanied by a meaningful improvement in profitability.
So, around 15% to 17% is a sustainable number, and we should target that.
We received certificate of suitability from EDQM for Fenofibrate-Process II, taking our total CEP approvals to 22.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25%+ (from 15-20%) with 14-15% EBITDA margin, after Q2 revenue rose ~40% YoY; backing is partly concrete (ethyl acetate debottlenecking done, 18,000 MTPA ibuprofen and CDMO projects due FY28, 90-95% utilisation) but the FY27 uplift rests mainly on pricing, mix and utilisation with no volume/price split given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin at 14-15% (H1 at 14.5%), targets 15-17% sustainable for FY29, and expects power, fuel and freight costs to ease in Q3-Q4 from the elevated 14.5% other-expense ratio.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Specialty chemicals toll plant is in trials with first batches expected Nov 2026, Ethyl Acetate debottlenecked to 1.2 lakh tonnes is done, and the 12,000 to 18,000 MTPA ibuprofen and CDMO projects are approved for FY28, though the brief notes CDMO commercialisation timing has already slipped.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ibuprofen and major products run at 90-95% utilisation and H2 is guided similar to H1 (~INR1,550 crore per half), with the FY27 25%+ growth figure given on a value basis and no volume/price split disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Three projects worth about INR500 crore were announced in Q2 and FY27 capex of INR250 crore is planned with about half spent in H1, so no new announcement is needed in the window and any further one would be a follow-on at 90%+ utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was just raised to 25%+ from 15-20% after H1 growth of about 39%, but management said H2 will be similar to H1, so a further raise depends on ibuprofen prices holding beyond the 1-2 quarters they guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ibuprofen prices are guided flat only for 1-2 quarters and the peer and China supply additions are a named risk, while raw material exposure (62-63% imported) and pass-through clauses are not fully in place.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty chemicals toll batches are expected in November 2026 and CDMO tablets (1,500 million per year, Europe-focused) are due for FY28 commercialisation, though CDMO needs about a year of customer validation.

rows.label: API customer onboarding and CDMO ramp
rows.why: API customer onboarding takes 6-8 months to start commercial orders and CDMO works with 2-3 mainly European customers, with validation about a year, so new revenue lands mostly after the window.

rows.label: No further borrowing; working capital peak INR200 crore
rows.why: Management said no further borrowing is planned and cash flow plus cash on hand are sufficient, with INR250 crore FY27 capex about half spent in H1.

rows.label: Ibuprofen prices flat for 1-2 quarters
rows.why: Prices have been stable for 2-3 quarters and are expected to hold for 1-2 more, but management would not forecast beyond that and peer supply is a watch item.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 performance, the raised FY27 guidance and the 15-17% FY29 margin target, but cautious and evasive on ibuprofen pricing beyond 1-2 quarters, CDMO margins and the volume/price split, while analysts pushed on those same points.
